Mass Effect

I had heard such good things about the game . . . but I just couldn't get into it. First off, the gameplay was a lesser derivative of stuff like Gears of War. Thus I was basically playing a worse version of another game, and the inventory system was pretty rough. Then there was stuff like driving around outside on that Hoth-like planet which wasn't especially good either, and it felt like so-so gameplay chucked in for the sake of variety.

Then there was the story and RPG elements. Some of the characters were really cool, to be fair. On the other hand, it took me out of the story hard when I realized that gaining rapport with your crew members was just a matter of paying attention and time to them. The underlying game systems were pretty transparent when you ended up talking to people for the sake of not missing content with them. Oh, and then it felt really game-y when the way you proved your investment in a character was by doing quests for them. Some of this is genre-standard stuff, but it was all the more reason that this game wasn't anything special.

To be fair, the ME1 wasn't very good compared to the rest of the franchise (and other games) now. Similar to Assassin's Creed, the first game was new and fresh enough to get people to notice, and then they really got things right with the second entry in the series.

Ultima 9. Oh man. I was so excited about Ultima 9. For no reason at all really. I never played any of the previous games. I was too young when they were released. But I just got really wrapped up in taking part in the epic conclusion to one of the pillars of gaming back in the 90's. Words almost fail to describe how utterly bland and terrible this game was. It shipped effectively broken it was so full of bugs. It was so bad, Origin shipped out a replacement install disc, with a free copy of Ultima Online and a free month of play time. Things only got worse when people found scraps of the original script for the game, dungeons that were cut, plot points that were left out but inadequately worked around.
